subject: Insurance
title: Germany: The Bismarck Model
description: A fast breakdown of Germany: The Bismarck Model for builders.

hook.text: Germany invented modern health insurance in 1883 under Otto von Bismarck. It's the oldest universal system in the world.

buildup.text: Germany uses nonprofit 'sickness funds.' Employers and employees split premiums. Over 100 funds compete for members.

discovery.text: Everyone must enroll. Funds can't deny anyone or charge based on health. Competition drives quality, not exclusion.

twist.text: Wealthy Germans can opt out into private insurance. About 11% do. Critics say this creates a two-tier system.

climax.text: Germany balanced competition with universal access. Multiple insurers, mandatory coverage, no one left behind.

quiz.question: When did Germany create its health insurance system?
